title: Paul McCartney holds auditions for guitarists | 1970
content:
Paul McCartney began holding two days of auditions for guitarists on 10 October 1970.

The auditions, for what would become the Ram album, were held in a loft on West 45th Street in Manhattan, New York City.

At the end of the two days, McCartney selected David Spinozza to play on the album. During his audition, Spinozza was asked to play chords from ‘Another Day’, which became the first track recorded during the sessions.

Honestly, when I got the call, I didn’t know it was an audition. It wasn’t couched like that. My wife said, ‘There’s a Linda on the phone, she wants to talk to you about a session.’ I just thought I was getting called for a recording session. She says, ‘Hi, this is Linda. We’d like to hear you play.’ I said, ‘What do you mean, you’d like to hear me play?’ And I said, ‘Who is this?’ She said, ‘Linda McCartney.’ And then it hit me, and I said, ‘Well, what do you do?’ She said, ‘Well, we’re staying in a loft on the West Side. Would you mind coming by?’ I thought it was an informal thing. You’d come by and you’d play with them.
David Spinozza, 15 June 2019
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair

The recording sessions for Ram began on 12 October 1970.
